title: Capacity Sentry: Autoscale Horizon, Burst Quarantine, and Soft-Isolation PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-level PRD for 'Capacity Sentry' — an integrated set of features for Dedicated capacity that balances predictable reserved throughput with safe transient burst behavior and tenant soft-isolation. This PRD covers requirements, acceptance criteria, UX, telemetry, rollout plan, and known trade-offs. The goal is to reduce noisy-tenant impact on reserved pools while preserving developer-friendly burstability and minimizing per-token cost increases.
problem_statement: Large tenants and spiky workloads occasionally exhaust reserved pool headroom, causing contention and tail latency regressions for co-located tenants. Current strategies either over-provision (high cost) or aggressively preempt bursts (poor UX). We need a mechanism that: 1) enforces per-tenant burst guardrails, 2) allows safe opportunistic borrow of buffer capacity, and 3) autos-scales reserved pools with a time-aware horizon to avoid thrash and surprise evictions.
goals: Provide configurable burst quarantine that contains individual tenant burst impact to a bounded window
Introduce an autoscale horizon that smooths scale-ups/downs and prefers proactive prewarm for predicted demand
Add soft-isolation controls (soft-evict, degrade, partial-throttle) so tenants can be deprioritized without full shutdown
Expose control plane and Console UX for tenants/operators to set policies per-reservation
Ship end-to-end telemetry and SLO guardrails so we can measure cost, latency, and customer impact
non_goals: Rewriting low-level runtime kernels; runtime optimizations will be incremental and coordinated with ENG
Replacing core billing model — we will surface metrics for billing but not change billing in this iteration
Implementing cross-region failover; this PRD focuses on single-reservation pools (zonal)
scope: In-scope: API extensions for ReservedPool configuration, a runtime admission controller that enforces burst-quarantine windows and credit accounting, autoscale controller with configurable horizon and cool-down, Console surfaces for policy editing and incident views, telemetry dashboards and alerting. Out-of-scope: KMS/HSM changes, on-prem packaging changes beyond control-plane flags, new pricing SKUs.
requirements: API: add fields to ReservedPool: autoscale_horizon_seconds (int), burst_quarantine_window_seconds (int), burst_credit_bucket_size (int), soft_isolation_mode (enum: off|degrade|throttle|soft-evict)
Runtime: admission controller must track per-tenant burst credits with O(1) check and bounded memory per tenant
Autoscaler: should evaluate headroom every minute and decide scale-up only when predicted 95th-percentile sustained demand > headroom for autoscale_horizon_seconds
Prewarm: when scale-up decision is made, prewarm instances asynchronously with a prioritized warm queue to avoid throttling spikes
Fallback: implement configurable fallback policies when pool exhausted (fallback_model_variant, fallback_region, enforce_rate_limit)
Console: policy editor, per-reservation summary, tenant-level burst history sparkline, simulated-effect tool to preview policy changes
Telemetry: token-level cost breakdown, per-tenant burst credit consumption time-series, pool headroom and pending-warm instances, P95/P99 latency heatmap per pool
Testing: unit tests for credit accounting, chaos tests that simulate multiple tenants bursting, and load-tests that evaluate autoscaler stability
acceptance_criteria: API: ReservedPool schema extended and backwards-compatible; create/update calls validate new fields and default behavior matches current (zero/disabled) settings
Runtime: under a 5-tenant synthetic workload where one tenant bursts 3x baseline for 90s, other tenants' median latency increases <10% with burst_quarantine_window_seconds set to 120
Autoscaler Stability: no more than 2 scale operations per 10-minute window under realistic traffic traces and autoscale_horizon_seconds=300

Soft-Isolation Modes: soft-evict should gracefully reduce a tenant to preconfigured baseline rate without dropping active connections; degrade should apply model-variant fallback within 15s of condition
Console: operator can edit policy and run simulation; simulation shows predicted headroom/eviction for the synthetic traces
Telemetry & Alerts: alerts fire when pool headroom < 10% for > 2m and when burst-credit depletion rate exceeds threshold; dashboards show per-tenant burst-credit consumption
Security: changes pass security review and threat model for per-tenant accounting data; sensitive logs masked
Documentation: PRD, API docs, Console help, and operator playbook (runbooks) published and linked in the ticket
design_decisions: Use token-based credit bucket for burst accounting instead of strict rate-limiter to preserve request ordering and KV-cache locality
Autoscale horizon chosen as a tunable parameter (default 300s) to balance reaction speed vs. oscillation
Prefer graceful degradation (model variant fallback) over hard preemption to keep customer apps available
Make soft_isolation_mode configurable per-reservation rather than global to allow customers with different SLAs
tradeoffs: Conservative horizons reduce thrash but increase time to adapt to sudden sustained demand — may require higher buffer heels
Credit accounting needs memory per tenant; to keep costs low we will evict cold tenant counters after TTL which can cause short-term inaccuracies
Prewarming increases short-term cost but reduces tail latency — we will expose prewarm aggressiveness setting to teams
Console simulation is approximate and based on sampled traces; it should not be the sole source for SLA guarantees
rollout_plan: Phase 1: API + telemetry + internal-only runtime (canary in staging) — 2 weeks. Phase 2: public beta for select Dedicated customers with opt-in flag and Operator playbook — 4 weeks. Phase 3: general availability with Console defaults and recommended presets — 2 weeks. Rollback: operator can disable autoscale and set burst_quarantine_window_seconds=0 to disable quarantine behaviors.
telemetry_and_alerting: Dashboard: ReservedPool Overview (headroom, pending-warm, P95/P99 latency), Tenant Burst Credits (consumption rate), Autoscale Decisions (timestamps and reasons)
Alert: BURST_CREDIT_STEADY_DEPLETION when any tenant consumes >80% of allocated burst credits over 5m (ops pager)
SLOs: maintain P95 generation latency within 1.2x baseline for non-bursting tenants
security_and_privacy_considerations: Per-tenant accounting data will be stored encrypted at rest with RBAC. Audit logs for actions that change reservoir or quarantine policies must include actor, timestamp, and before/after snapshots. We will coordinate with Security to validate that concession of soft-isolation data does not leak customer usage patterns across tenants.
open_questions: Should we offer per-tenant configurable burst credits or only per-reservation buckets?
What is the right default burst_credit_bucket_size for small vs. large reservations?
Do we need billing changes for prewarm costs or will we absorb prewarm until usage stabilizes?
How aggressive should automatic prewarm be for bursty customers vs. predictable steady ones?
acceptance_test_plans: Unit tests for credit bucket increment/decrement and TTL eviction
Integration test: 10k synthetic QPS mix with one tenant bursting; measure latencies and credit usage
Chaos test: forcibly kill prewarm workers to validate fallback paths
E2E: create ReservedPool with policies via API and exercise Console simulation, then run live load against canary pool
